The counter serves one student at a time; the next student starts immediately after the previous finishes. If a student arrives after the counter would be free, they wait until their arrival time.

Students (name, arrivalMinute, serviceSeconds):
Mia, 0, 45
Noah, 0, 60
Olivia, 0, 30
Liam, 1, 50
Emma, 1, 40
Ava, 2, 55

Note: arrival times are in whole minutes; convert everything to seconds (minute 0 = 0 sec, minute 1 = 60 sec, etc.).

Print one line per student in the order listed: "<name> <startSec> <endSec>" where startSec is when they begin being served and endSec is when they finish, both in seconds from noon.

After all students, print one line: "IDLE <seconds>" where seconds is the amount of time (in seconds) between the last student finishing and the moment 5 minutes (300 sec) after noon, i.e., how long the counter sits unused before the 300-second mark. If the last student finishes after 300 sec, print "IDLE 0".

Print 7 lines total, no extra spaces.
tasks.category: scheduling and simulation with a fixed timeline of events (queues, timers, resource use)

tasks.title: Robot Warehouse Pick Queue
tasks.prompt:
A robot in a warehouse processes pick requests from a queue. There are 5 pick stations numbered 1-5, each initially holding 0 items. The robot starts at station 1. Requests arrive in a fixed order; each request specifies a target station and a number of items to pick. Travel between adjacent stations takes 2 seconds; travel between non-adjacent stations takes 2 seconds per step (e.g., station 1 to station 4 = 6 seconds). Picking takes 1 second per item. The robot processes requests strictly in order (no reordering).

Station inventory (items available at each station):
Station 1: 4
Station 2: 0
Station 3: 6
Station 4: 3
Station 5: 2

Requests (targetStation, itemsToPick):
1. Station 3, 2 items
2. Station 5, 1 item
3. Station 2, 3 items
4. Station 4, 2 items
5. Station 1, 5 items

A request fails if the station does not have enough items; a failed request takes 0 pick time but the robot still travels to the station (and stays there for the next request).

Start time is 0 seconds. Print one line per request: "REQ<n> <ok|fail> <endTime>" where n is the request number (1-5) and endTime is the robot's clock in seconds after completing (or failing) that request.

After all requests, print one line: "REMAIN <total>" where total is the sum of items left across all 5 stations.

Print 6 lines total, no trailing spaces.
tasks.category: scheduling and simulation with a fixed timeline of events (queues, timers, resource use)

tasks.title: Bakery Oven Batch Scheduler
tasks.prompt:
A bakery has 2 ovens (Oven 1, Oven 2). Each oven can bake one batch at a time. Batches arrive at fixed times (minutes) and each has a bake duration (minutes) and a designated oven preference. If the preferred oven is busy when the batch arrives, the batch waits for that oven (it never switches to the other oven). A batch starts at max(arrivalTime, preferredOvenFreeTime).

Batches in arrival order:
1. Bread, arrive 0, bake 20 min, Oven 1
2. Cake, arrive 5, bake 35 min, Oven 2
3. Muffins, arrive 10, bake 15 min, Oven 1
4. Pie, arrive 25, bake 25 min, Oven 1
5. Cookies, arrive 30, bake 10 min, Oven 2
6. Rolls, arrive 40, bake 20 min, Oven 2

Print one line per batch: "<name> <oven> <startMin> <endMin>" where oven is 1 or 2, startMin is when baking begins, and endMin is when it finishes.

After all batches, print one line per oven: "OVEN<n> <busyMin>" where busyMin is the total minutes that oven spent baking (sum of durations of batches it actually baked).

Print 6 + 2 = 8 lines total, no extra spaces.
tasks.category: scheduling and simulation with a fixed timeline of events (queues, timers, resource use)

tasks.title: Laundry Room Machine Timers
tasks.prompt:
A shared laundry room has 3 washing machines (M1, M2, M3). Each machine runs one load at a time. Loads arrive at fixed times (minutes) and each has a wash duration (minutes). Machines are assigned in strict round-robin order (M1, M2, M3, M1, M2, ...) to arriving loads regardless of whether the machine is free; if the assigned machine is busy, the load waits until that machine frees up.

Loads in arrival order:
1. Towels, arrive 0, 30 min
2. Shirts, arrive 5, 25 min
3. Jeans, arrive 8, 40 min
4. Socks, arrive 15, 20 min
5. Sheets, arrive 20, 35 min
6. Uniforms, arrive 25, 25 min

Start time is 0. For each load, startTime = max(arrivalTime, assignedMachineFreeTime), endTime = startTime + duration. Update that machine's free time to endTime.

Print one line per load: "<name> <machine> <startMin> <endMin>".

After all loads, print one line per machine in order M1, M2, M3: "<machine> <idleMin>" where idleMin is the total minutes that machine sat free between time 0 and the moment the last load in the whole system finished (the global end time). A machine's idle time = globalEndTime - (sum of its load durations) - (time before its first load started, if any). More precisely: idleMin = globalEndTime - (its first load's start time) - (sum of its load durations).

Print 6 + 3 = 9 lines total, no extra spaces.
tasks.category: scheduling and simulation with a fixed timeline of events (queues, timers, resource use)

tasks.title: Swim Meet Lane Rotation
tasks.prompt:
A swim meet has 4 lanes and runs 5 heats. Swimmers are assigned to lanes for each heat. Heat results (lane, swimmerName, timeSeconds) by heat:
Heat 1: Lane1 Zoe 32, Lane2 Yan 29, Lane3 Wren 35, Lane4 Xander 31
Heat 2: Lane1 Yan 30, Lane2 Wren 33, Lane3 Xander 28, Lane4 Zoe 34
Heat 3: Lane1 Wren 31, Lane2 Xander 36, Lane3 Zoe 27, Lane4 Yan 32

Heat 5: Lane1 Zoe 31, Lane2 Yan 33, Lane3 Wren 30, Lane4 Xander 35

After all 5 heats, compute each swimmer's total points. Print one line per swimmer sorted by total points descending; ties broken alphabetically by name ascending: "<name> <totalPoints>".

Also track the single fastest swimmer overall (lowest time in any heat; ties broken by earliest heat, then lowest lane). Print a final line: "FASTEST <name> <timeSeconds>".

tasks.prompt:

Write a program that lists every distinct color arrangement of these 4 bushes in the row, one per line, and then prints how many distinct arrangements there are.

Output format:

- Print the arrangements in lexicographic order (comparing the full space-separated string, so "Pink Red Red White" comes before "Red Pink Pink White").

where N is the count.

Write a program that prints every possible path from start to finish, one per line, followed by the total number of paths.

- Print the paths in lexicographic order (so "DDRR" comes before "DRDR").

  Total paths: N
where N is the count.

tasks.title: Board Game Piece Placements
tasks.prompt:
In a board game, 4 identical wooden tokens are to be placed on 4 marked spots in a line. The spots are numbered 1 through 4. Instead, consider this variant: you have 6 spots numbered 1 through 6 and you must choose 4 of them to receive a token, then place the tokens in increasing spot order.

Write a program that prints every subset of 4 spots (out of 6) as a space-separated increasing list, one per line, then prints the count.

Output format:
- Print each subset as its spot numbers in increasing order separated by a single space, e.g. "1 2 3 4".
- Print subsets in lexicographic order of their printed form (so "1 2 3 5" comes before "1 2 4 5").
- After all subset lines, print one line of the form:
  Total selections: N
where N is the count.

tasks.title: Beekeeper Flower Patch Tours
tasks.prompt:
A beekeeper's bee visits 4 flower patches in a row, visiting each exactly once. The patches are named: Daisy, Dandelion, Rose, Daisy. Two patches named "Daisy" are indistinguishable.

Write a program that prints every distinct visiting order of the 4 patches, one per line, then prints the count.

Output format:
- Print each order as its patch names separated by a single space, e.g. "Daisy Dandelion Daisy Rose".
- Print orders in lexicographic order.

  Distinct tours: N
where N is the count.

tasks.title: Print Shop Ink Coverage Matrix
tasks.prompt:
A small print shop estimates ink usage per page for four different paper types based on two print modes. The shop has recorded the ink units used per page (in milliliters) in a 2x4 matrix, where each row is a print mode and each column is a paper type.

Ink matrix (rows = modes, columns = paper types):
Mode 0, Paper A: 0.12
Mode 0, Paper B: 0.18
Mode 0, Paper C: 0.09
Mode 0, Paper D: 0.15
Mode 1, Paper A: 0.25
Mode 1, Paper B: 0.31
Mode 1, Paper C: 0.20

The shop also has an order quantity matrix of the same shape, giving how many pages of each paper type will be printed in each mode:
Order matrix:
Mode 0: 120, 80, 200, 50
Mode 1: 60, 40, 100, 30

Write a program that computes:
1. Total ink used in Mode 0 (sum over all paper types of ink*pages).
2. Total ink used in Mode 1.
3. Total ink across both modes.
4. The paper type (column index 0-3) that consumed the most ink across both modes combined.

Mode0: <total ink, 2 decimal places>
Mode1: <total ink, 2 decimal places>
Total: <total ink, 2 decimal places>
TopPaper: <column index 0-3>

tasks.title: Greenhouse Plant Height Grid
tasks.prompt:
A greenhouse keeps a 3x3 grid of planters. Each planter contains a plant whose height is measured in centimeters. The heights are stored in a 3x3 matrix (rows 0-2, columns 0-2):

Row 2: 8, 20, 14

The greenhouse also applies a growth factor to each row (multiplied after measurement): Row 0 factor 1.1, Row 1 factor 1.3, Row 2 factor 0.9.

Write a program that:

2. Finds the maximum adjusted height across all 9 planters.
3. Finds the row index (0-2) with the largest total adjusted height across its 3 columns.

Max: <maximum adjusted height, 1 decimal place>
TopRow: <row index 0-2>
Over20: <count>

tasks.title: Robot Grid Turn Matrix
tasks.prompt:
A robot on a grid can move in 4 directions: 0=North, 1=East, 2=South, 3=West. A 4x4 turn-cost matrix C[i][j] gives the cost in seconds for the robot to change from facing direction i to facing direction j:
C =
[0, 2, 4, 2]
[2, 0, 2, 4]
[4, 2, 0, 2]
[2, 4, 2, 0]

The robot executes a sequence of facing directions it must adopt in order: [0, 1, 1, 3, 2, 0]. The total turn cost is the sum of C[seq[t]][seq[t+1]] for each consecutive pair in the sequence.

Write a program that:
1. Computes the total turn cost for the given sequence.
2. Finds the maximum single turn cost encountered in the sequence.
3. Counts how many turns in the sequence cost exactly 2 seconds.
4. Finds the direction (0-3) that appears most frequently in the sequence (ties: report the smaller direction index).

Total: <total turn cost, integer>
MaxTurn: <maximum single turn cost, integer>
Count2: <number of turns costing 2>
FaceDir: <direction index 0-3>

tasks.title: Vending Machine Price Matrix
tasks.prompt:

[95, 130, 175]

Write a program that:

MaxCost: <maximum total cost, integer>

tasks.title: Garden Drip Line Pressure Matrix

[120, 125, 125]

Write a program that:

tasks.title: Robot Warehouse Orientation Matrix
tasks.prompt:
A warehouse robot's orientation is described by a rotation matrix R that rotates points by an angle. The robot starts at orientation R0 (identity) and applies a sequence of 90-degree rotations. Represent orientation as a 2x2 integer matrix.

[0, 1]

[0, 1]
[-1, 0]

Write a program that:

Offset: <x,y as integers with a comma, no spaces>
Manhattan: <integer>
SameAsStart: <YES or NO>

[14, 16, 15, 17]

Write a program that:

tasks.title: Train Route Transfer Cost Matrix
tasks.prompt:
A regional train operator has 5 stops numbered 0-4. A fare matrix F[i][j] gives the cost in dollars for a ticket from stop i to stop j (F[i][i] = 0, and some pairs have no direct service, shown as 0):

[0, 3, 0, 5, 0]
[3, 0, 4, 0, 7]
[0, 4, 0, 6, 0]
[5, 0, 6, 0, 8]
[0, 7, 0, 8, 0]

A traveler wants to go from stop 0 to stop 4. They can take a direct ticket if available, or a one-transfer ticket via one intermediate stop k (k not 0 or 4): cost = F[0][k] + F[k][4].

Write a program that:
1. Finds the cheapest total fare from stop 0 to stop 4 considering direct and all one-transfer options.

3. Finds the stop (0-4, excluding 0 and 4) that would serve as the cheapest single-transfer intermediate stop (smallest index if tied). If no one-transfer route exists, output NONE.

MaxDirect: <most expensive direct fare, integer>

tasks.title: Robot Warehouse Zone Distances
tasks.prompt:

[20, 8, 0, 10]
[15, 18, 10, 0]

TotalDist: <total travel distance, integer>

FarthestZone: <zone index 0-3>
Dist10Pairs: <count of unordered pairs with distance 10, integer>
